{{nihongo|'''Samuta Shrine'''|寒田神社}} is a [[shinto shrine]] in the [[Engishiki Jinmyōchō]]. It is located in [[Sagami Province]].

It is regarded as one of the thirteen Engishiki shrines (small shrine) of {{ill|Sagami Province|ckb|پارێزگای ساگامی|cs|Provincie Sagami|de|Provinz Sagami|es|Provincia de Sagami|fa|ولایت ساگامی|fr|Province de Sagami|gl|Provincia de Sagami|id|Provinsi Sagami|it|Sagami (provincia)|ja|相模国|ko|사가미국|lt|Sagamio žemė|nl|Sagami (provincie)|pt|Província de Sagami|ru|Сагами (провинция)|simple|Sagami Province|sk|Sagami (provincia)|sr|Провинција Сагами|tr|Sagami (vilayet)|uk|Провінція Саґамі|zh|相模國|zh_min_nan|Sagami-kok|zh_yue|相模國|qid=Q1053732}} listed in the ''{{ill|Engishiki Jinmyōchō|abstract|Q11064932|fr|Engishiki Jinmyōchō|ja|延喜式神名帳|simple|Engishiki Jinmyōchō|zh|延喜式神名帳|qid=Q11064932}}'' of {{ill|927|Q30470|qid=Q30470}} ({{ill|Enchō|Q1327274|qid=Q1327274|lt=Encho}} 5). Its precincts face the {{ill|Sakawa River|arz|نهر ساكاوا|de|Sakawa (Fluss)|fa|رود ساکاوا|ja|酒匂川|zh|酒匂川|qid=Q11644295}}.

=== History ===
Founded in the era of {{ill|Emperor Nintoku|Q313119|qid=Q313119}}. It is mentioned in ancient {{ill|Fudoki|ca|Fudoki|de|Fudoki|es|Fudoki|fa|فودوکی|fr|Fudoki|id|Fudoki|it|Fudoki|ja|風土記|ko|풍토기|no|Fudoki|pl|Fudoki|ru|Фудоки|sr|Фудоки|uk|Фудокі|zh|風土記 (日本)|qid=Q1194534}}. It was formerly also called Sagamita Shrine, Sabuta Shrine, and Samuta Shrine. In the ''{{ill|Engishiki Jinmyōchō|abstract|Q11064932|fr|Engishiki Jinmyōchō|ja|延喜式神名帳|simple|Engishiki Jinmyōchō|zh|延喜式神名帳|qid=Q11064932}}'' it appears as "Sagami no kuni, Ashigami District, Samuta Shrine, small." In the Edo period it was also called Samuta Shrine Kanda Daimyojin{{efn|In ''{{ill|Shinpen Sagami no Kuni Fudoki-kō|Q11503942|qid=Q11503942}}'' it is written as Kanda Myojinsha{{sfn|新編相模国風土記稿 松田惣領 神田明神社}}.}}.

According to shrine tradition, Yamato Takeru stayed here for a while during his eastern expedition. It is said that when he prayed here for success, he poured sake into the Sakawa River, and when he returned after the campaign, the fragrance of sake still remained, so the river came to be called Sakawa. A wooden bowl said to be from that event is preserved at the shrine.

It was rebuilt in {{ill|1868|Q7717|qid=Q7717}} ({{ill|Keiō|Q776775|qid=Q776775}} 4). It became a {{ill|Gō-sha|Q134917316|qid=Q134917316}} in {{ill|1874|Q7761|qid=Q7761}} ({{ill|Meiji era|Q3125096|qid=Q3125096}} 7), and a {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Prefectural Shrine}} in {{ill|1941|Q5231|qid=Q5231}} ({{ill|Shōwa era|Q327567|qid=Q327567}} 16). Later, in {{ill|1968|Q2644|qid=Q2644}} (Showa 43), it was designated by the Kanagawa Prefectural Association of Shinto Shrines as a {{ill|Kanagawa Prefecture Shrine Office Designated Shrine|Q11588941|qid=Q11588941|lt=shrine visited by imperial envoy for offerings}}, and in {{ill|1971|Q2475|qid=Q2475}} (Showa 46) it was designated a {{ill|Historic site|Q1081138|qid=Q1081138}} by Matsuda Town.

=== Rituals ===
* {{ill|Reisai|Q11385469|qid=Q11385469|lt=Grand annual festival}} (July 31)
** The mikoshi procession was designated a Matsuda Town {{ill|Intangible Cultural Property (Japan)|Q2901957|qid=Q2901957}} in 1971 (Showa 46).
** In the past, the annual festival was held on the last day of June each year.

=== Other ===
*{{ill|John Glenn|Q182642|qid=Q182642|lt=John Glenn}}, the {{ill|Astronaut|Q11631|qid=Q11631}} who first succeeded in orbiting the {{ill|Earth|Q2|qid=Q2}} for the {{ill|United States|Q30|qid=Q30}}, carried a Samuta Shrine prayer talisman during spaceflight and visited the shrine in thanks after returning to Earth.

=== Access ===
* 5-minute walk from {{ill|Matsuda Station|Q5357522|qid=Q5357522}} on {{ill|Central Japan Railway Company|Q513679|qid=Q513679}} {{ill|Gotemba Line|Q667927|qid=Q667927}}.
* 7-minute walk from {{ill|Shin-Matsuda Station|Q4419978|qid=Q4419978}} on {{ill|Odakyu Electric Railway|Q83584|qid=Q83584}} {{ill|Odakyū Odawara Line|Q135176|qid=Q135176|lt=Odawara Line}}.
* About 10 minutes by car from {{ill|Oi-Matsuda interchange|Q10933470|qid=Q10933470}} on the {{ill|Tōmei Expressway|Q1135694|qid=Q1135694}}.
